sn4.25:1.2: Amending _Arati_ to _Rati_ (“delight”), following the argument in Marcus Bingenheimer, *Studies in Āgama Literature* 4.5.
sn4.25:2.2: Mara’s fascination with the Buddha was more than professional, He was the original stalker.
sn4.25:3.4: At this point, Māra has given up hope.
sn4.25:14.1: The Buddha’s responds more closely to the accusations than he did with Māra. | This verse is quoted and discussed, and the Sutta cited by name as the “Maiden’s Questions” (_kumāripañhā_) at [an10.26]().
sn4.25:16.2: Bodhi notes that the Sanskrit parallels here have present tense _tarati_ for the Pali’s aorist _atari_. I translate assuming present tense. | Here the five floods must be the five senses, against which the Buddha has proven himself immune. Delight wants to know how to transcend the mind.
sn4.25:17.2: The present participle _asaṅkharāno_ is a unique form. The meaning is not entirely clear in this context. The commentary says it means not generating the three kinds of kamma that lead to rebirth.
sn4.25:24.1: I find this metaphor hard to understand. The verse bears some resemblance to SN 36.4, where the patala is said to be under the ocean. I assume it means you’re trying to swim with a rock on your head!
